text:
incident-bot: Automated alert: synthetic-canary-runner-a is failing >50% over last 5m from EU region. Failure type: 429/backpressure. PagerDuty incident created: INC-3050

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty - Incident INC-3050 fired (High) · 3 pages attempted. Acknowledgement required.

alex: acked. I'm on-call (eu-sre). Starting triage. :eyes:

jamie: saw the same in dashboards. spikes of 429s starting ~5m ago. latency also up for canary responses.

alex: thinking two possibilities: backend service under load or the canary runner is overwhelmed (timeouts/backpressure). I'll check runner logs and queue depth.

sre-runner-bot: canary-runner-a logs (tail -n 50):
```
2026-03-15T09:12:01Z INFO request id=abc123 start
2026-03-15T09:12:02Z ERROR upstream returned 429 repeated=3 svc=nlp-model shards=4
2026-03-15T09:12:04Z WARN queue_len=120 worker_idle=0
2026-03-15T09:12:10Z ERROR upstream returned 429 repeated=5 svc=nlp-model
```

jamie: queue_len 120 is suspicious — our runners usually keep <20. Looks like congestion inside the canary pool.

alex: prioritizing mitigation to stop noisy pages. Two immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily mute the PagerDuty alert rule for this specific probe while we mitigate, 2) scale canary-runner horizontally. Thoughts?

sana: +1 to mute to stop page storms. But we should note that muting loses coverage; only mute the specific synthetic check ID. I'll prepare a brief incident note for PD muting.

mira: customer impact assessment — so far we have no correlating increase in user-facing errors. This looks isolated to synthetic probe traffic hitting a stressed staging-like model endpoint. But tagging as potential impact until confirmed.

alex: executing scale: `kubectl scale deployment/canary-runner-a --replicas=5 -n synth` — increasing from 2->5. Also bumping worker concurrency to 8 in configmap. Pasting command and plan.

jamie: running the scale now, watching metrics. If 429 rate drops -> good. If not, we fallback to throttling the probe (lower RPS) and add retry/backoff.

sre-runner-bot: kubectl output: scaled deployment "canary-runner-a" to 5 replicas

(2m later)

jamie: metrics show queue_len decreasing to ~15, 429 rate falling from 52% -> 8% across the pool. Latency improving.

alex: nice. I'm going to silence the PagerDuty rule for synthetic-canary-eu->canary-runner-a for 30m to avoid noise; leaving PD escalation for any other infra alerts.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty - Silence applied to rule synthetic-canary-eu for 30 minutes by alex.

sana: adding a short runbook note: reduce synthetic RPS by 60% for the next 10m as a precaution, then ramp slowly. Also scheduling a post-incident task to add circuit-breaking on canary->model calls.

mira: customer impact update: Verified no customer 5xx spikes or support tickets in the window. Marking as no customer impact but elevated risk.

alex: handoff to jamie for watch. I'll be available if it re-escalates. jamie, take PD ack and status.

jamie: taking watch. Will post updates every 10m or on change. :thumbsup:

(10m later)

jamie: follow-up: system stable, 429s back to baseline (~1-2%), queue_len steady ~10, latency normal. I've scheduled canary RPS ramp plan and a follow-up retrospective.

sana: opened ticket INFRA-4521: add circuit-break & backoff in canary client; also recommend autoscale policy on canary-runner to react to queue_len. Assigned to eng-runtime.

mira: documenting incident summary in incident tracker: root cause likely synthetic runner under-provisioned and bursty probe rate hitting a partially overloaded model variant. No direct customer impact.

alex: closing PD incident INC-3050. Leaving the PagerDuty silence to expire. Thanks all for quick triage.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty - Incident INC-3050 closed by alex.

jamie: postmortem owner? I can take it with sana. We'll include measurement of probe RPS patterns and a new autoscale threshold.

sana: adding postmortem notes now. Also will propose a guardrail: auto-mute synthetic rule after 3 pages if no customer impact and status is 'synthetic-only'.

alex: good idea. Re-opening alerts if any downstream user-facing error occurs. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
